title: Factor a semistable marked modification through a finite normal target
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^	imes$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve [def-trf-multipointed-curve] with smooth generic curve $X_\eta$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and etale generic marking $D_\eta$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $f:(Y,E)	o(X,D)$ be a semistable $\eta$-modification [def-trf-multipointed-curve-modification]. Let $
u:N	o X$ be the relative normalization of $X$ in $X_\eta$ [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization], defined on an affine open by the integral closure of its coordinate ring in the regular functions on its generic fibre. Then $N$ is normal (each local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]), flat and finitely presented over $T$ of pure relative dimension one; $
u$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and is an $\eta$-modification, and $N_\eta\simeq X_\eta$. Let $D_N$ be the schematic closure of $D_\eta$ in $N$ (the closed subscheme defined by functions whose restriction to $D_\eta$ is zero). Then $(N,D_N)$ is a multipointed $T$-curve and $
u$ extends to an $\eta$-modification of pairs $
u:(N,D_N)	o(X,D)$. There is a factorization of pairs $f=
u\circ g$ with $g:(Y,E)	o(N,D_N)$ a semistable $\eta$-modification; the source curve and its marking are unchanged. For every $t\in T$ and every irreducible component $C$ of $Y_t$, $f_Y(C)$ is a singleton if and only if $g_Y(C)$ is a singleton. The same equivalence holds for every irreducible component after any geometric base change $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega	o T$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Here semistability, $\eta$-modification and schematic density have precisely the meanings of [def-trf-multipointed-curve-modification], and components have the meaning of [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Temkin, Lemma 4.4.4 proof, first sentence (printed p. 31); Lemma 4.4.1(i) (printed p. 30) for finite presentation of the normalization, and Remark 4.1 (printed pp. 24--25) for the schematic-closure marking. The last contraction equivalence is the finite-fibre irreducibility argument explained in report.md. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The base $T$ is normal integral and affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Indeed every localization $V_{\mathfrak p}$ is again a valuation domain: for an element of $K^\times$ one of it and its inverse already belongs to $V$. A valuation domain is integrally closed: if $z$ is integral but outside it, $z^{-1}$ is in its maximal ideal, and division of a monic equation by the highest power of $z$ puts $1$ in that maximal ideal. The generic point is a principal open. If $V=K$ take $a=1$; otherwise take $0\ne a$ in its least nonzero prime. Every nonzero prime contains $a$, so $D(a)=\eta$ and $V[1/a]=K$. For each flat $T$-scheme used below, [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] applied to its structure sheaf makes multiplication by $a$ injective on every affine open. Thus localization into its generic fibre is injective, and that generic open is schematically dense. This applies to $X,D,Y,E$ and subsequently to $N,D_N$.

source.place: Section 4 preamble, printed p. 24; finite-height principal generic open and schematic-density calculation (agent expansion).

proof.text:
Apply the first assertion of [lem-trf-valuation-curve-projective-preparation] to the $T$-curve $X$: all valuation hypotheses agree, and $X_\eta$ is smooth. It gives a finite $\eta$-modification $X^
u	o X$ with normal source, which is flat and finitely presented of pure relative dimension one. We identify this absolute normalization with the specified relative normalization $N$. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, flatness gives $A\hookrightarrow A_K$ by Step 1. The reducedness and finite-component assertion of [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models], together with the dense generic open from Step 1, shows that the irreducible components of $X$ and of $X_\eta$ have the same generic points. Its generic affine open is smooth over $K$, so its local rings are normal by [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal], and it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product], $A_K$ is a finite product of integrally closed domains $C_i$. Thus the component function fields are $\operatorname{Frac}C_i$. An element of their product integral over $A$ is integral over $A_K$ as well; coordinatewise normality puts it in every $C_i$, hence in $A_K$. Conversely an element of $A_K$ integral over $A$ is integral in the product of these fraction fields. The two integral closures therefore coincide. Their affine normalization maps agree with the charts of [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]; these canonical identifications glue over $X$. Hence $N=X^
u$, proving all the asserted normality, finiteness, flatness, finite presentation, relative dimension and generic-fibre claims for $N$ and $
u$. No integrality of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.1(i), printed p. 30, including the equality of relative and absolute normalization for smooth generic fibre; affine equality expanded by the agent.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models] to $(X,D)$ and the reduced modification $
u:N	o X$ of Step 2. Normality makes $N$ reduced, and $
u$ is an $\eta$-modification. Its marking assertion says exactly that the schematic closure of $D_\eta$ in $N$ is a flat finitely presented marking of pure relative dimension zero, and that $(N,D_N)	o(X,D)$ is an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves. It is the $D_N$ in the statement, since the cited closure is defined by the same restriction kernel. We shall also need $
u_D:D_N	o D$ to be finite. The generic marking lies in $N	imes_XD$, so every local equation defining that closed subscheme vanishes on $D_\eta$ and hence on its schematic closure $D_N$. Thus $D_N\hookrightarrow N	imes_XD$ is a closed immersion. The projection $N	imes_XD	o D$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). Over an affine of $D$ it is a finite algebra, and its quotient defining $D_N$ is still generated by the images of the same finite module generators. Therefore $
u_D$ is finite, and is proper and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper].

source.place: Remark 4.1, printed pp. 24--25; the finite marking map is the affine quotient calculation for the normalization map.

proof.text: The source $Y$ is normal. To prove this without assuming strict semistability, apply [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-eta-normal] to the semistable multipointed curve $(Y,E)$ over the normal integral qcqs base $T$ from Step 1. Its statement explicitly includes this semistable instance and gives that $Y$ is $\eta$-normal. Since $f_\eta$ is an isomorphism, $Y_\eta\simeq X_\eta$ is smooth. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-curve-projective-preparation] to the $T$-curve $Y$. Its normalization $Y^\nu\to Y$ is a finite $\eta$-modification with normal source. By $\eta$-normality it is an isomorphism, so $Y$ itself is normal.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20--21, and Lemma 4.4.1(i), printed p. 30; normality underlying the first sentence of Lemma 4.4.4.

proof.text:
The normal-source factorization assertion of [lem-trf-valuation-curve-projective-preparation] now applies to $f_Y:Y	o X$: it is an $\eta$-modification with normal source by Step 4. With the identification $N=X^
u$ of Step 2 it gives a morphism $g_Y:Y	o N$ satisfying $
u g_Y=f_Y$. This morphism is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated], applied over $X$: $Y	o X$ is proper and $N	o X$ is separated since it is proper. Its generic fibre is $
u_\eta^{-1}f_{Y,\eta}$, an isomorphism. The generic opens of $Y$ and $N$ are schematically dense by Step 1, so $g_Y$ is an $\eta$-modification of curves.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4 proof, first sentence, printed p. 31; Stacks Tag 01W6, proper source to a separated target.

proof.text:
Let $h:E\hookrightarrow Y\xrightarrow{g_Y}N$. Its generic fibre is the prescribed inclusion of $D_\eta$ into $N_\eta$. Every section of the ideal of $D_N$ therefore pulls back to zero on the generic open of $E$. Since that open is schematically dense by Step 1, the pulled-back section is zero. The kernel-ideal factorization assertion [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel](2) gives a unique $g_D:E	o D_N$ with $h=i_Ng_D$. This use is legitimate on every affine open of $N$: the relevant ideal is contained in the kernel of the map to sections on its inverse image in $E$. Moreover $h$ is quasi-compact: $E$ is quasi-compact, and $N$ is quasi-separated, so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) applies. The equality $
u_Dg_D=f_D$ follows by composing the marking square and cancelling the closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] over $D$, $g_D$ is proper, since $f_D$ is proper and $
u_D$ is separated by Step 3. It is an isomorphism on the generic fibre. Its generic source and target are schematically dense by Step 1. Thus $g=(g_Y,g_D)$ is an $\eta$-modification of pairs, and both marking and curve equations give $f=
u\circ g$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4 proof, first sentence and Remark 4.1; Stacks Tag 01R8 (kernel-ideal factorization) and Tag 01W6 (properness).

proof.text: Semistability is a condition on the source pair: the geometric curve fibres are nodal or smooth, and the marking is etale and lies in the smooth locus, as in [def-trf-multipointed-curve-modification]. The construction of $g$ has changed neither $Y$ nor $E$ nor its closed immersion into $Y$. Thus the same semistable source pair makes $g$ a semistable $\eta$-modification. This establishes the required factorization with the source and its marking unchanged.

source.place: Section 1.2, printed p. 2 (semistable modification); Lemma 4.4.4 proof, first sentence.

proof.text:
Fix $t\in T$ and an irreducible component $C$ of $Y_t$. If $g_Y(C)$ is one point, then $f_Y(C)=
u(g_Y(C))$ is one point. Conversely suppose $f_Y(C)=\{x\}$. The image $g_Y(C)$ is a nonempty irreducible subset of the topological fibre $
u^{-1}(x)$. That fibre is finite discrete: over an affine neighbourhood of $x$, the finite map $
u$ is given by a finite algebra $A	o B$, and the fibre algebra $B\otimes_A\kappa(x)$ is finite over the field $\kappa(x)$ (tensor the finite set of module generators). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] with this field as the zero-dimensional local base. The fibre-prime correspondence of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] identifies these points with the points of $N$ over $x$ and preserves specialization. Since all the fibre primes are maximal, no two distinct points of this finite subspace specialize to one another; it is therefore discrete. A nonempty irreducible subset of a finite discrete space has exactly one point. Hence $g_Y(C)$ is a singleton. For any algebraically closed $\Omega$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega	o T$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a) makes $
u_\Omega:N_\Omega	o X_\Omega$ finite. The same argument applies to every irreducible component of $Y_\Omega$ and the equation $f_\Omega=
u_\Omega g_\Omega$. This proves the geometric-base-change assertion without assuming that an original component stays irreducible after extension.
